subject: Chemistry
title: How Instant Ice Packs Work
description: A quick win: understand How Instant Ice Packs Work.

hook.text: Squeeze an instant ice pack and it turns cold in seconds—no freezer needed. Just chemistry.

buildup.text: Inside the pack are ammonium nitrate crystals and a separate pouch of water.

discovery.text: Squeezing breaks the water pouch. Ammonium nitrate dissolves and absorbs heat from the surroundings—endothermic reaction.

twist.text: The temperature drops to about 2°C in under a minute. No ice, no fridge—just dissolving salt.

climax.text: Hot packs work the opposite way: calcium chloride dissolves exothermically, releasing heat.

punchline.text: Salt dissolves, steals heat. Instant cold from a chemical reaction.

quiz.question: Why does an instant ice pack get cold?
options: Ammonium nitrate dissolving absorbs heat in an endothermic reaction
Compressed air expands and cools inside the pack
A chemical reaction produces ice crystals

details.summary: Instant ice packs contain water and ammonium nitrate separated by a barrier. When squeezed, the barrier breaks and ammonium nitrate dissolves in the water in a highly endothermic reaction that absorbs heat from the surroundings.
details.whyItMatters: Ice packs demonstrate endothermic dissolution, a thermodynamic concept where the entropy gained by dissolving the salt outweighs the energy cost of breaking crystal bonds.
takeaways: Dissolving ammonium nitrate absorbs heat from the surrounding water
The process is an endothermic reaction driven by entropy increase
Hot packs use an exothermic reaction like calcium chloride dissolving

faq.question: Why does ammonium nitrate make the water cold when it dissolves?
faq.answer: Breaking the ammonium nitrate crystal lattice requires more energy than is released when ions are hydrated by water molecules. The net energy deficit is drawn from the thermal energy of the water, lowering its temperature. The reaction proceeds because the entropy increase favors dissolution.

faq.question: How do instant hot packs work if ice packs use endothermic reactions?
faq.answer: Hot packs typically use calcium chloride or magnesium sulfate, which dissolve exothermically, releasing heat into the water. Some hot packs use supersaturated sodium acetate that crystallizes when triggered, releasing stored energy as heat from an exothermic crystallization process.
